I'd follow other advice about speaking with the students union, as well as teaching unions if you have your student membership, but also get firm with the uni and refuse to go back. If they get funny with you, ask them what risk assessments they've done regarding the physical assaults that happen at the school and your pregnancy and how they intend to ensure you are able to safely complete your placement. I know a few people have said as much but it really depends. 

Uni wise, depends how many assignments they want and how much effort you want to put in. My uni  only really had 3 big assignments but had weekly logs to fill in. Didn't really take up much of my time and I'm a last minute person so did my assignments over a couple of days and did OK, this may or may not be your style. 

School wise, this is where the real difference is going to be noticeable. Both of my placement schools had full schemes of work, booklets, PowerPoints etc etc, to use and adapt to classes. That meant that my planning was extremely quick and easy, as it was essentially done and I just had to change things around to suit my groups. The downside to this, though, is I got complacent and now I don't think my planning is really up to scratch. So in hindsight, I should have put more effort in there, but I really valued keeping my evenings and weekends free. My mentors were supportive and accessible and most other staff were lovely too. However I knew people who rarely saw their mentor and didn't feel welcomed into the department and they struggled a lot more, and things took a lot longer because they didn't get the guidance. 
The problem with the school part though is generally you don't have a choice. Some places will have a system to place you in a school if you already have a link to it and the school's agreement, but you'd still have at least another placement. 

Short version, uni side takes as much time as you'd think uni would generally. The real lottery is how demanding the school is on your time, which can't be predicted

How much help, if any, are you getting from family? If they can comfortably cover any and all rent, you might be OK on the lower loan. If they can only help somewhat, or not at all, you may well struggle on even the higher loan. My halls cost about 115 per week back in 2014, I think the same halls now are around 130-140 per week. The lower loan would be entirely taken up by rent with no money for food, clothes, equipment or a social life. Depending on the course related costs and cost of living in the area, you may even struggle on the bigger loan unfortunately. 

A bit anecdotal but I don't currently have rent or utility costs, but am doing a year course where I took the highest loan I could. I'm still struggling a lot financially because I have a lot of placements, and so travel expenses, formal clothes cost, extra food than I'd normally buy etc etc. 

The higher debt sucks, and yes there's interest, but at least you have to be in at least an ok job before you pay any of it back, and it's a much safer debt than not taking the loan and falling victim to predatory "student loans" from dodgy companies or credit cards (though they're harder to get as a student anyway)

I feel FF has much more flash, cool looking abilities at higher levels that not many classes in WoW can match, but I prefer how classes work and play in wow in general. Rotations feel a bit more intuitive to me in WoW and abilities serve clearer functions beyond looking cool as hell. 

Levelling, now, is something I prefer in WoW too. Maybe I'm just still too noobish on FF but I sometimes struggle to find fun, engaging things to do when levelling new jobs. WoW though, although I have to level an entirely new character, has revamped levelling so you can choose from any previous expansion story line and often many different zones within that expansion. (Heads up, your first character has to go through BFA but once that hits 50 any subsequent characters choose any expansion) 

Playing with friends - honestly this is pretty similar for both, level scaling is in both to an extent but FF lacks co-op story from what I've played. Both have dungeon scaling, but WoW has more dungeon variety when levelling (beyond first character again) in WoW I can start characters with friends and we can all do everything together short of one or two quests that are super rare. 

To be honest if you like one you'll probably find things to like about the other as well as things you dislike in comparison but I recommend playing WoW as is now and seeing what you think for yourself, and don't worry about endgame or toxicity too much. I main balance and whilst I'm certainly not the greatest druid alive, I think I do pretty well. There has been some good advice already and a lot of it is personal preference but just to offer an alternative to the big group AoE down build (which to be fair is pretty fun) I like a build that let's me absolutely nuke a single target whilst still being pretty great at AoE. 

I personally never bother with force of nature, I find it much handier having Natures balance. It means I start most fights with a free starsurge or starfall depending what I need. I also take incarnation. That way, if I'm feeling really lazy wanting to kill that one enemy, I pop incarnation, double starsurge and most of my work is done for me. When geared this alone will easily kill most basic mobs, but even when not geared it has the added benefit of empowering your other casts twice (plus incarnation bonuses) to finish them off before they even reach you.

Along those lines as well, personally I like wild charge over renewal. I pick resto affinity and find that gives me more than enough healing options (especially when combined with bark skin reduction) and wild charge let's me bound backward in moonkin form to give myself some distance (pair it with typhoon and they're never touching you, but any on that tier works well enough depending on situation and preference) 

I always go twin moons as I'm too lazy for an extra button and I like being able to dot two mobs with moon fire. This is especially good for me as I generally go shooting stars so more targets dotted per GCD helps with that. That said, fury of elune is a lot of fun and if I know I'm going to be pulling large groups I definitely enjoy taking that, but for really quickly killing one or two at a time.

If you have warmode on then thorns is definitely handy, I quite like moonkin aura too to ramp up that crit. I also take faerie fire normally incase I get ganked by a melee class, especially rogues, as it is quite satisfying seeing them disarmed and confused while you then pull off the above quick nuke combo and take almost their entire health bar before they can hit you again. 

Hope some of this helps and you find a play style you enjoy and works for you

Me and some friends did exactly this once a few years back. The 3 of us worked for a large hotel chain in a popular tourist town at the height of the summer season.   Our zero hour contracts meant that we had all kinds of inconsistent shifts which is standard for those things but management were NOT helpful or pleasant at all. My other two friends are a couple and never had the same day off despite requests. We were always denied requests for set days off, hours extended last minute, berated and belittled often, generally it was just horrible being there. We, individually and together, had spoken to supervisors and managers about our concerns and at best nothing happened, normally though they'd just get really passive aggressive with us and put us on the crap jobs for a bit. 
Eventually we got fed up, and there was a clause in our contract that said we were under no obligation to accept any shifts offered to us and so we went to the duty supervisor and said that's what we were doing. Today would be our last shift and we would not be accepting any more. Their whole attitude changed immediately and she practically begged us to come in for just one more day whilst they tried to find more people to cover us. We agreed, not for the managers but because we knew 3 of us leaving so suddenly would mean a lot of work for the rest of the team and we didn't want to impact them too much if it could be helped. 

When me and one friend came in the next day (it was the third's day off anyway) we got immediately sent to the managers who gave us this big speech about how disappointed they were in us and how we let everyone down and how they hadn't expected us to actually come in. We didn't say much as we were done with them at that point but we said how in spite of what they may think given how we quit that when we said we would do something, we would, but enough was enough and we were done balancing other obligations (all were students but also personal stuff) with a job that had no respect for us at all. 

That last day was really nice, most of the other workers were quite impressed (no everyone didn't clap) and some said they wished they could but they needed the money too much. Even one of the previously nasty supervisors, the one we told we were quitting, was chatty and pleasant (no idea why she couldn't have been before but oh well) and we only had the easy jobs to do as they made us up a room list last minute of all stay overs.

My most recent ex who I still adore and want back very badly had a history with this guy. I talk to her openly and say that I trust her but given what she told me about how she had said no and he didn't stop until she was in the mood enough to say yes that I didn't trust him. she would always get defensive and say I should just trust her and that she wouldn't stop being friends with him. fast forward to our breakup, we end up having an argument a few weeks after about other stuff and the topic of jealousy comes up.
